# Pandamonium v1.0.48

This release makes the composer quieter and more capable at the same time: the selected model and its effort/reasoning control now stay visible together instead of hiding inside the switching list. It also lands the first accessibility-scale controls, right-docked Settings and Updater panels, reorderable sidebar buckets, durable provider context windows so a restart no longer drops a connected model back to the conservative fallback budget, and the JOS duty-pack layer that mounts protocol rules by intent with a real token budget.

## MAD-891 — Protocols 2/4: mount duty packs (P2–P7 and IPAV) by intent with real token budget

### Problem

The core JOS pack from Protocols 1/4 applied everywhere, but the domain-specific rules — context, memory, actions, authority, learning, observability, and inspect-plan-act-verify — were not mounted at runtime, so turns had no way to receive only the protocol guidance their intent needed while respecting a token budget.

### Implementation

Added the JOS-P2..P7 and IPAV duty packs with domain manifests. `src/protocol_registry.py` selects packs by intent domain and renders them after the always-mounted core packs in one marked block with a declared token budget, dropping overflow packs while keeping core. The agent prompt builder and chat path classify the latest message and pass the intent domain; trivial turns mount core only. The manifest parser now supports inline domain lists.

### Product value and UI visibility

Every agent and chat turn now carries the exact protocol guidance for its intent (shell actions get authority and action rules, research gets context rules, and so on) without spending context on unrelated domains. The JOS-P7 trace records which pack ids were mounted per turn.

### Verification

`tests/test_protocol_duty_packs.py` covers the mount matrix, declared body-budget honesty, trace references, and budget-driven drops; the protocol registry, mounting, and agent identity suites were rerun. The full Python suite passed (5,651 passed, 5 skipped) on the merged branch.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Controlled by the existing protocol layer setting; disabling it restores core-only behavior. Pack bodies are asserted to fit their declared `token_budget`, and no data, schema, or authentication behavior changed.

### References

- [Linear MAD-891](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-891/protocols-24-mount-duty-packs-p2-p7-and-ipav-by-intent-with-real-token)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/89)

## MAD-903 — Models: persist and auto-resolve provider catalog context windows per connected model

### Problem

Provider catalog discovery already read `context_length` from the connected endpoint's `/models`, but the discovered map was in-memory and fetched lazily. A process restart or a transient fetch failure dropped a model back to "unknown" and the conservative 6000-token budget even though the provider reported a real window.

### Implementation

Discovered windows are now persisted per endpoint in `data/model_context_catalog.json` with an atomic write that stores only endpoint, model id, and window — no secrets. Resolution precedence is operator override (`model_context_windows`) -> persisted catalog -> live catalog -> built-in known table -> conservative unknown fallback. For api/proxy endpoints the provider catalog wins over a stale known-table entry, with the table still the fallback when the endpoint reports nothing. A per-test isolation fixture keeps the store out of the repository data directory.

### Product value and UI visibility

Model budget behavior stays consistent across restarts and transient network failures, so conversations get the context the provider actually supports instead of an artificially small budget. Persisted rows are proven values, so restarts no longer reset the budget silently.

### Verification

Red-first and regression tests in `tests/test_model_catalog_persistence.py` cover precedence, persistence, restart survival, and sanitizer rejection; related budget, context, and cache tests were rerun. The full Python suite passed (5,644 passed, 5 skipped) on the merged branch.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

The catalog file is created at runtime and contains no credentials; deleting it removes the optimization with no migration or data loss. Existing settings, conversations, and operator overrides are untouched. No new dependency was added.

### References

- [Linear MAD-903](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-903/models-persist-and-auto-resolve-provider-catalog-context-windows-per)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/83)

## MAD-898 — UI: collapse model picker and put reasoning control in the composer

### Problem

The open model picker always rendered the full identity list plus the effort card, and the effort control was only reachable inside that menu. Once an identity was selected the composer still read as a list rather than one compact control.

### Implementation

The effort card moved out of `#model-picker-menu` into a composer popover anchored inside `#model-picker-wrap`. A compact chip (`#composer-effort-btn`) shows the current value (`#composer-effort-value`) and toggles the popover; `conversationContext.js` keeps the existing applicability logic (Codex reasoning for pc-codex, rounds budget for Jarvis), refreshes the chip label with the slider, and closes the popover on outside click, Escape, or when the picker opens. The picker menu now only lists identities for switching.

### Product value and UI visibility

The collapsed composer shows the selected identity and its effort/reasoning value side by side. Opening the picker is now purely a switching action, and the effort slider stays one click away without hunting through a list. The popover uses a fixed bottom-sheet position on phones.

### Verification

Source guards in `tests/test_model_selector_compact.py` assert the card sits outside the menu and the chip wiring exists. `tests/browser/m7-codex-workspace.spec.js` was updated to open the chip for Codex model/reasoning flows, and `tests/browser/mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js` exercises the composer controls. 243 static/UI Python guards and 34 focused browser tests pass.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only change: selection, routing (`agent_target`, model PATCH), keyboard navigation, and toasts are unchanged. The chip hides for contexts without an applicable effort control. No dependency or schema change.

### References

- [Linear MAD-898](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-898/ui-collapse-model-picker-and-put-reasoning-control-in-the-composer)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/86)

## MAD-899 — UI: quick visual batch — orb symmetry, update card, right-dock panels, UI scale, bucket reorder

### Problem

The access shield orb was visibly smaller than the voice orb; the sidebar update card was bulky with stacked full-width buttons; Settings and the Updater opened centered instead of where the rest of the workspace panels live; text and icons were hard to read with no independent size controls; and sidebar buckets could not be reordered even though sessions and projects could.

### Implementation

The access orb now matches the voice orb at 38px with a scaled glyph. The update card uses a single row of actions and ellipsized metadata while keeping readable type sizes. Settings and the Updater call the existing right-edge dock on open (the updater loads `modalSnap.js` at runtime so the release-bridge harness can still embed the file). The UI text scale was generalized to steps 90/100/110/125/140 with shared zoom compensation, and a new independent `--ui-icon-scale` variable scales sidebar and navigation glyphs. Settings > Appearance and the Theme popup expose both controls, persisted locally. The five sidebar buckets carry hover drag handles and persist their order through the existing section-order storage.

### Product value and UI visibility

Panels open where users expect them, the update card reads cleanly, the two orbs are symmetric, text and icons can be enlarged independently for accessibility, and any bucket — including Email above Chats — can be moved and stays put across reloads.

### Verification

`tests/browser/mad-899-ui-batch.spec.js` covers orb symmetry, right-docked Settings and Updater, text/icon scale application and persistence, and drag-reorder persistence. The updater, access-mode, and M7 selector/workspace browser specs pass, the release-bridge harness passes, and 243 static/UI Python guards pass.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

All new preferences are client-local (`odysseus-ui-scale`, `odysseus-ui-icon-scale`, `sidebar-section-order`); no server schema or data migration. Text scaling reuses the existing CSS zoom mechanism with per-step viewport compensation, so a zoomed modal header stays reachable. Motion-sensitive and mobile behavior are unchanged.

### References

- [Linear MAD-899](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-899/ui-quick-visual-batch-orb-symmetry-update-card-right-dock-panels-ui)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/86)
